  "/health-library/womens-health/menstrual-health/menstrual-health": "Menstrual Health The Menstrual Cycle — Your Body's Vital Sign Menstruation (a \"period\") is the monthly shedding of the uterine lining when no pregnancy occurs. But a period is more than just bleeding — it is the visible end of a complex hormonal cycle that affects your energy, mood and health every single day. Leading medical organisations including the American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists now recognise the menstrual cycle as a vital sign, just like pulse or blood pressure. Normal Cycle Facts - Average cycle: 28 days (21–35 days is normal for adults) - Bleeding lasts: 3–7 days - Blood loss: 30–80 mL (2–6 tablespoons) - Flow heaviest: first 1–2 days - Key is regularity for you — not matching a textbook average The Hormonal Symphony Hypothalamus → releases GnRH → Pituitary → releases FSH & LH → Ovaries → produce estrogen & progesterone → Feedback loop, also influenced by thyroid and adrenal glands. Stress, illness and sleep can disrupt this entire chain. Cycle as Vital Sign An irregular or painful cycle can signal underlying conditions including: hormonal imbalances (thyroid, PCOS); bleeding disorders; structural issues (fibroids, polyps); infections or inflammatory conditions (endometriosis). Tracking it is not just about knowing your next period date — it is about understanding what your body is telling you. 💡 Start Tracking Today Track your cycle on a calendar, in a notebook or with an app. Note the dates, flow level, type of pain and how it affects your life. This is your evidence — bring it to a provider. You are the expert on your own body. The Four Phases of Your Cycle Phase 1 — Menstruation (Days 1–5) Estrogen and progesterone drop sharply. The uterine lining has no hormones to sustain it, so it breaks down and sheds — this is your period. Triggered by the collapse of the corpus luteum. Cramping · Fatigue · Low back pain Phase 2 — Follicular Phase (Days 1–13, overlaps with menstruation) FSH stimulates several follicles (tiny sacs containing eggs) to mature. One becomes dominant and produces increasing amounts of estrogen, thickening the uterine lining. Energy slowly returns. Energy returns · Mood lifts · Skin clears Phase 3 — Ovulation (Around Day 14 in a 28-day cycle) Estrogen peaks → LH surge → dominant follicle releases a mature egg. The egg lives 12–24 hours after release. Sperm can survive up to 5 days — so the fertile window is ~6 days total. Mittelschmerz · Clear stretchy mucus · Higher libido Phase 4 — Luteal Phase (Days 15–28) The empty follicle becomes the corpus luteum, producing large amounts of progesterone to prepare the uterine lining for possible pregnancy. If no pregnancy, the corpus luteum degenerates, progesterone falls and the cycle begins again. PMS symptoms · Bloating · Breast tenderness · Mood shifts Signs of Ovulation — How to Recognise It Sign What It Looks Like How to Track Cervical mucus Clear, slippery, stretchy like raw egg white — \"EWCM\" (egg white cervical mucus) is the most fertile sign Check daily with toilet paper or clean fingers Basal body temperature (BBT) Temperature rises slightly (0.3–0.6°C) after ovulation due to progesterone — confirms ovulation already occurred, does not predict it Take temperature every morning before getting out of bed with a BBT thermometer Ovulation pain (Mittelschmerz) Mild twinge or cramp on one side of lower abdomen — lasts minutes to hours Note in diary or app — the side alternates each month Ovulation predictor kits (OPKs) Detect the LH surge that happens 24–36 hours before ovulation Available at pharmacies; urine test similar to a pregnancy test Menstrual Hygiene & Products Product How to Use It Important Notes Pads Apply to underwear; change every 4–6 hours or more if flow is heavy Wrap used disposables and bin them — never flush. Avoid scented varieties. Tampons Insert into vagina; change every 4–8 hours; use the lowest absorbency that works for your flow Never wear a single tampon for more than 8 hours — reduces risk of Toxic Shock Syndrome (TSS) Menstrual Cups/Discs Insert and seal; rinse after each use; at end of period, sanitise by boiling in water for 1–2 minutes Reusable and cost-effective. Emptying twice daily is usually sufficient. Takes practice to master. Period Underwear Change every 6–12 hours (more if flow is heavy); rinse immediately after removing; machine wash per instructions Higher upfront cost but washable and reusable. Good for backup or light days. Self-Care for Cramps & Pain Heat Therapy Use a hot water bottle, heating pad or warm bath with Epsom salts on your lower abdomen. Be careful not to burn yourself — prolonged exposure to a heat source can cause Erythema Ab Igne (EAI), a skin rash from repeated heat exposure. OTC Medication Ibuprofen is often better for cramps than paracetamol because it reduces prostaglandins (the chemicals that cause the uterus to contract). Buscopan can also help. Always take with food and at the recommended dose — if your prescribed dose isn't working, tell your provider rather than taking more. Movement & Massage Light yoga, stretching or walking can ease pain and boost mood by releasing endorphins. Gentle circular massage on your lower back can relax tight muscles. Exercise may feel like the last thing you want to do — but gentle movement genuinely helps. Period Problems: Bleeding Issues Period problems are any changes or symptoms related to your menstrual cycle that cause discomfort, disrupt your life or signal an underlying health condition. Up to 1 in 5 people with uteruses will experience a menstrual disorder at some point. Dismissing severe period pain as \"just part of being a woman\" is the single biggest reason conditions like endometriosis go undiagnosed for years. Your pain is valid. 1. Heavy Menstrual Bleeding (Menorrhagia) Signs of Heavy Bleeding - Soaking through a pad or tampon every hour for several consecutive hours - Needing to \"double-up\" on protection - Passing large blood clots — bigger than a 10-shilling coin - Bleeding lasting more than 7 days - Feeling tired, short of breath or lightheaded (signs of iron-deficiency anaemia) Normal average: 2–5 moderately soaked pads per day. Using more than 5–6 fully soaked pads is considered heavy. Causes & Treatment Causes: Hormonal imbalances; uterine fibroids; uterine polyps; adenomyosis; bleeding disorders (von Willebrand disease); certain medications (blood thinners). Medications: - Tranexamic acid — reduces blood loss by helping clots form - NSAIDs (ibuprofen) — reduce pain and can slightly decrease flow - Hormonal options — pills, hormonal IUD, progestin tablets - Iron supplements — often needed if anaemic 2. Irregular Periods (Oligomenorrhea) Cycles that are consistently longer than 35 days or very unpredictable. Occasional irregularities are common during stress or illness. Consistent irregularity (month after month) needs investigation. Common Causes: Stress; extreme exercise; eating disorders (low body weight); PCOS; thyroid disorders (under- or overactive); perimenopause (transition to menopause). Normal in the First Years: In the first 1–2 years after your first period (menarche), cycles are often irregular as the body learns to ovulate. This is completely normal. By age 16, cycles should generally be predictable. 3. Absent Periods (Amenorrhea) Type Definition Common Causes Primary Amenorrhea No period by age 15 Hormonal disorders; structural abnormalities; genetic conditions Secondary Amenorrhea Missing periods for 3+ months after having regular cycles Pregnancy (most common) · PCOS · thyroid disorder · high prolactin · low body weight · excessive exercise · premature ovarian insufficiency · pituitary tumours ⚠️ Important If you have missed your period for 3 months and are not pregnant, you need an evaluation. Prolonged absence of periods can lead to bone density loss (osteoporosis) over time because estrogen is essential for bone maintenance. This risk is real even in young women. 4. Bleeding Between Periods (Intermenstrual Bleeding) Any bleeding that happens outside your regular period always has a cause — sometimes benign, but always requiring investigation. Type Notes Mid-cycle spotting (around Day 14) Can be normal ovulation spotting — track for 2+ cycles; see provider if heavy After sex (post-coital bleeding) Could be cervical issues (infection, polyp, inflammation) — requires evaluation Caused by infections (cervicitis, STIs) Requires STI testing and treatment Cervical or uterine polyps/fibroids Usually benign but needs confirmation by ultrasound or hysteroscopy Cervical or uterine cancer Less common but serious — any unexplained intermenstrual bleeding requires investigation After menopause — any amount URGENT — any post-menopausal bleeding requires immediate evaluation Period Pain: Dysmenorrhea Primary Dysmenorrhea — \"Normal\" Cramping Cause: Prostaglandins — chemicals that make the uterus contract to shed its lining. Highest on Day 1 of your period (which is why cramps are often worst then). Feels like: Dull, throbbing cramping in the lower abdomen, radiating to lower back and thighs. When: Starts just before or with your period, lasts 1–3 days. Response: Usually responds well to OTC pain relief (ibuprofen better than paracetamol — targets prostaglandins). Secondary Dysmenorrhea — Pain Caused by a Condition Cause: An underlying reproductive disorder — most commonly endometriosis, fibroids, adenomyosis or PID. Feels like: Sharp, stabbing or persistent pain that may be present even when not on your period. When: Often starts earlier in the cycle, lasts longer, and does not respond well to OTC painkillers. Action needed: Requires medical investigation. Bring a pain diary to your appointment — note timing, severity (1–10) and impact on your life. Kenya Myth-Busting: Period Problems ❌ Myth ✅ Truth \"If you have period pain, just bear it — it means you are a 'real woman'\" Pain that stops you from functioning is a medical symptom, not a rite of passage. Severe pain can be a sign of endometriosis that requires treatment. \"Heavy bleeding is just how you are — some women bleed more\" Bleeding heavy enough to cause anaemia or interfere with life is a medical problem, not a personality trait. \"Herbs can 'clean' the womb and fix irregular periods\" Irregular periods are caused by hormonal or structural issues. Herbs cannot fix a hormone imbalance or shrink a fibroid. Relying on herbs delays proper diagnosis. \"You cannot get pregnant if your periods are irregular\" Irregular periods mean you ovulate unpredictably, not that you never ovulate. You can still get pregnant — you still need contraception. \"Period blood is dirty blood that needs to be expelled\" Menstrual blood is the same blood in your body, mixed with uterine tissue. It is not \"dirty\" or \"toxic.\" PMS & PMDD — The Pre-Menstrual Phase PMS is incredibly common — up to 75% of people who menstruate experience some form. PMDD is a severe, debilitating version affecting 3–8%. PMDD is recognised as a psychiatric condition — the brain has an abnormal reaction to normal hormonal changes. It is not a character flaw or weakness. Feature PMS PMDD Number of symptoms One or more At least 5 (including at least 1 mood symptom) Mood impact Mild to moderate Severe — disrupts relationships, work and school Anger/Irritability Can occur, but manageable Intense rage, anger, relationship conflict Depression/Anxiety Mild Severe, hopeless, overwhelmed, panicky Functioning Able to function normally Unable to function; needs to isolate Duration A few days before period 1–2 weeks before period, relief after period starts Key diagnostic clue Predictable pattern each cycle A \"week of relief\" after period starts — then symptoms return next luteal phase PMDD Core Symptoms (DSM criteria — must include ≥1 of first 4) Must Include at Least One of These Four: 1. Marked mood swings (sudden sadness, tearfulness) 2. Marked irritability or anger 3. Marked depressed mood, feelings of hopelessness 4. Marked anxiety, tension, feeling \"on edge\" Additional Possible Symptoms: 5. Decreased interest in usual activities 6. Difficulty concentrating 7. Fatigue, lack of energy 8. Changes in appetite (overeating or specific cravings) 9. Hypersomnia (too much sleep) or insomnia 10. Feeling overwhelmed or out of control 11. Physical symptoms (breast tenderness, bloating, headaches) What Causes PMS & PMDD? People with PMS/PMDD have normal levels of estrogen and progesterone. The problem is how their brain and body react to these normal fluctuations. Hormonal changes may trigger a drop in serotonin — the brain chemical regulating mood, sleep and pain. Genetics play a role: if your mother or sister had PMDD, you are more likely to have it. Management & Treatment Lifestyle (First-line for mild–moderate PMS) Nutrition: Eat complex carbs (boost serotonin); increase calcium to 1,200 mg/day — studies show significant reduction in PMS symptoms (sources: milk, yoghurt, leafy greens, fortified plant milks); limit salt (reduces bloating); reduce caffeine and alcohol (worsen anxiety and breast tenderness). Exercise: Regular aerobic activity releases endorphins, improves mood and reduces fatigue. Sleep: Aim 7–9 hours; consistent bedtime helps regulate mood. Stress management: Yoga, meditation, deep breathing, journaling. Medical Treatments (for PMDD or severe PMS) SSRIs (antidepressants) — the first-line treatment for PMDD. Fluoxetine or sertraline can be taken continuously or only during the luteal phase (1–2 weeks before period). Work within days for PMDD (faster than for depression). Hormonal birth control — pills suppressing ovulation (e.g., those containing drospirenone and ethinyl estradiol) can eliminate the hormonal cycle that triggers PMDD symptoms. GnRH agonists — In severe cases, temporarily induce menopause to stop the hormonal cycle. Usually short-term. ⚠️ When to Seek Urgent Help - If you have thoughts of self-harm or suicide related to your cycle — this is a medical emergency - Mood symptoms are affecting your relationships, work or ability to function - You feel hopeless, overwhelmed or out of control - Lifestyle changes are not helping after 2–3 cycles 💡 Diagnosing PMDD — The 4-Step Approach 1. Track symptoms daily for at least two cycles — note mood, physical symptoms and severity. 2. Look for the pattern — do symptoms appear 1–2 weeks before your period and disappear after it starts? 3. Book an appointment with a gynaecologist, psychiatrist or primary care provider. Bring your symptom tracker. 4. Be specific: Say \"I think I may have PMDD because my symptoms follow this pattern and they are severely affecting my life.\"",

Leading medical organisations including the American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists now recognise the menstrual cycle as a vital sign, just like pulse or blood pressure. For many young people in Kenya, this transition can be confusing, especially without accurate information. At the same time, threats to safety — in schools and communities — are real. Knowledge is your best protection. What Is Puberty? The time when your body matures from a child to an adult. Usually starts between ages 8–14 for girls and 9–15 for boys. These changes are driven by hormones — chemical messengers produced by glands in your body. Article 53 — Kenya Constitution Every child in Kenya has the right to be protected from abuse, neglect and all forms of violence under Article 53 of the Constitution and the Children Act, 2022. Puberty does not give anyone permission to touch you without your consent — your body belongs to you at every age. 💡 Key Point Knowledge is your best protection. Understanding your body helps you recognise when something is wrong. Knowing your rights helps you speak up. Understanding consent helps you set boundaries. Body Changes for Girls Everyone develops at their own pace. Your friend may start her period at 10 and you may not start until 14 — both are normal. Comparing yourself to others only causes unnecessary worry. Change What Happens When (Typical Age Range) Breast development (Thelarche) Small buds form under the nipple, then breasts grow. Usually the first visible sign of puberty. 8–13 years Pubic hair growth (Pubarche) Hair appears on the vulva, then underarms. Driven by adrenal androgens (adrenarche). 8–14 years Growth spurt Rapid increase in height — slows significantly after menarche begins. 9–14 years First period (Menarche) Menstruation begins — usually 2–3 years after breast budding. Cycles may be irregular for the first 1–2 years. 10–16 years (average 12.5) Vaginal discharge Clear or whitish fluid appears — the vagina cleaning itself. Often 6–12 months before first period. Typically before menarche Hips widen Body prepares for future childbearing — changes in fat distribution. Throughout puberty Body odour Sweat glands become more active — especially in armpits. Daily bathing and deodorant help. Throughout puberty ⚠️ Important — When to Seek Evaluation - Signs of puberty before age 8 — should be evaluated for precocious puberty - No breast development by age 13 — requires evaluation for delayed puberty - No period by age 15 (primary amenorrhea) — requires medical evaluation - It can take up to 5 years for cycles to become regular after menarche Body Changes for Boys Change What Happens When Testes & scrotum grow Usually the first visible sign of puberty in boys 9–14 years Penis grows Lengthens and thickens 10–15 years Pubic hair grows Hair appears at base of penis, then spreads to armpits, face, legs 9–15 years Voice deepens Voice may \"crack and break\" as the larynx grows — temporary and normal 10–15 years Growth spurt Rapid increase in height; shoulders broaden; muscle mass increases 10–16 years Wet dreams (nocturnal emissions) Ejaculation during sleep — involuntary and completely normal. Not a sign of anything wrong. 11–16 years ✨ Good to Know Wet dreams are completely normal. They do not mean you are \"bad\" or that something is wrong. It is your body's way of releasing excess semen. This is a natural part of male puberty that happens to almost all boys. Vaginal Discharge: What's Normal? One of the first signs of puberty in girls is vaginal discharge — fluid that comes from the vagina. This can be alarming if you don't expect it. It is completely normal and a sign of a healthy vagina doing its job. Normal Discharge - Clear or white (like egg whites or milk) - No strong smell (or very mild) - May stain underwear — slightly acidic, bleaches fabric (use panty liners if it bothers you) - Changes throughout the menstrual cycle: stretchy and clear around ovulation; thicker and whiter before period See a Provider If 🚨 Seek care if discharge is: - Yellow, green, or grey - Has a strong, foul or fishy smell - Accompanied by itching, burning or swelling around the vulva - Causing pain when urinating - Frothy or looks like cottage cheese A simple swab test gives the diagnosis. 💡 A little discharge is normal — it is the vagina cleaning itself. But if it changes colour, smell or causes discomfort, see a healthcare provider. Poor toilet hygiene is a common cause of irritation in young girls. Always wipe from front to back to prevent bacteria from the anus reaching the vagina. Menstruation: What to Expect What Happens During a Period - The uterine lining sheds because no pregnancy occurred - Bleeding typically lasts 3–7 days - Flow is heaviest in the first 1–2 days - Cycles may be irregular for the first 1–2 years — normal - Average blood loss: 30–80 mL (about 2–6 tablespoons) Common Period Symptoms - Cramping in lower belly - Backache - Bloating - Mood changes - Fatigue Mild discomfort is common. Pain that stops you going to school or living your life is NOT normal and deserves medical attention. 🇰🇪 Kenya Context — Menstrual Dignity A study in Kibera found that while 80% of school-going adolescent girls know menstruation is normal, many still lack access to clean water and private sanitation facilities at school. This makes managing periods with dignity difficult. If your school lacks facilities, speak to a teacher or parent — you have a right to learn in dignity. Hygiene During Puberty For Girls - Change sanitary pads every 4–6 hours (more often if flow is heavy) - Wash the vulva with water only — no soap inside - Wipe front to back after using the toilet - Wear breathable cotton underwear - Dispose of used pads properly — wrap and bin, don't flush For Boys - Wash the penis gently with water and mild soap - If uncircumcised, gently pull back foreskin and clean underneath - Change underwear daily For Everyone: - Shower or bathe daily, especially after sports - Use deodorant if body odour bothers you - Wash hands after using the toilet Body Autonomy: I Own My Body Body autonomy means your body belongs to you. No one else has the right to touch it, use it, or make decisions about it without your permission — at any age, in any situation. 4 Key Principles of Body Autonomy 1. You are the boss of your body. No one — not a relative, teacher, friend or stranger — has the right to touch you in ways that make you uncomfortable. 2. Consent must be freely given. Saying \"yes\" because you're scared, pressured or tricked is NOT real consent. 3. Consent can be withdrawn anytime. Even if you said yes before, you can change your mind. 4. You have the right to say \"NO.\" A simple \"No\" is enough — you don't need to explain. Safe Touch vs Unsafe Touch Safe Touch: Feels good, caring, helpful. Characteristics: respectful, not secret, not threatening. Examples: A parent helping you bathe when young; a doctor examining you with a parent present; a welcome hug; a pat on the back. Unsafe Touch: Feels scary, confusing or painful. Characteristics: secret, forced, makes you feel dirty or scared. Examples: Anyone touching your private parts; being asked to touch someone else's private parts; kisses that make you uncomfortable; being shown sexual pictures. ✨ Good to Know — Body Part Names Protect Children Teaching children the proper names for body parts (penis, vagina, breasts, bottom) is protective — not shameful. Abusers often target children who do not have words for their body parts, making it harder for the child to report what happened. Naming is a safety tool. The No-Go-Tell Rule Step 1 — NO Say \"No\" loudly and clearly. \"Stop that!\" \"I don't like that!\" \"Don't touch me!\" You do not need to be polite — say NO firmly. Step 2 — GO Get away from the situation as quickly as possible. Run to a safe place. Leave immediately — do not wait to see what happens next. Step 3 — TELL Tell a trusted adult until someone helps you. Keep telling until someone believes you and takes action. Do not give up. 💡 Safe Secrets vs Unsafe Secrets Safe secrets can be kept (like a surprise birthday party). Unsafe secrets that make you feel bad, scared or confused should never be kept — tell a trusted adult immediately. Knowledge is your best protection. What Is Puberty? The time when your body matures from a child to an adult. Usually starts between ages 8–14 for girls and 9–15 for boys. These changes are driven by hormones — chemical messengers produced by glands in your body. Article 53 — Kenya Constitution Every child in Kenya has the right to be protected from abuse, neglect and all forms of violence under Article 53 of the Constitution and the Children Act, 2022. Not a sign of anything wrong. 11–16 years ✨ Good to Know Wet dreams are completely normal. They do not mean you are \"bad\" or that something is wrong. It is your body's way of releasing excess semen. This is a natural part of male puberty that happens to almost all boys. Vaginal Discharge: What's Normal? One of the first signs of puberty in girls is vaginal discharge — fluid that comes from the vagina. This can be alarming if you don't expect it. It is completely normal and a sign of a healthy vagina doing its job. ✅ Normal Discharge - Clear or white (like egg whites or milk) - No strong smell (or very mild) - May stain underwear — slightly acidic, bleaches fabric (use panty liners if it bothers you) - Changes throughout the menstrual cycle: stretchy and clear around ovulation; thicker and whiter before period 🚨 See a Provider If: - Discharge is yellow, green, or grey - Discharge has a strong, foul or fishy smell - You have itching, burning or swelling around the vulva - You have pain when urinating - Discharge is frothy or looks like cottage cheese - Any of these symptoms appear — a simple swab test gives the diagnosis 💡 Key Point A little discharge is normal — it is the vagina cleaning itself. But if it changes colour, smell or causes discomfort, see a healthcare provider. Poor toilet hygiene is a common cause of irritation in young girls. Always wipe from front to back to prevent bacteria from the anus reaching the vagina. Menstruation: What to Expect What Happens During a Period - The uterine lining sheds because no pregnancy occurred - Bleeding typically lasts 3–7 days - Flow is heaviest in the first 1–2 days - Cycles may be irregular for the first 1–2 years — normal - Average blood loss: 30–80 mL (about 2–6 tablespoons) Common Period Symptoms - Cramping in lower belly - Backache - Bloating - Mood changes - Fatigue Mild discomfort is common. Pain that stops you going to school or living your life is NOT normal and deserves medical attention. 🇰🇪 Kenya Context — Menstrual Dignity A study in Kibera found that while 80% of school-going adolescent girls know menstruation is normal, many still lack access to clean water and private sanitation facilities at school. No one else has the right to touch it, use it, or make decisions about it without your permission — at any age, in any situation. 4 Key Principles of Body Autonomy 1. You are the boss of your body. No one — not a relative, teacher, friend or stranger — has the right to touch you in ways that make you uncomfortable. 2. Consent must be freely given. Saying \"yes\" because you're scared, pressured or tricked is NOT real consent. 3. Consent can be withdrawn anytime. Even if you said yes before, you can change your mind. 4. You have the right to say \"NO.\" A simple \"No\" is enough — you don't need to explain. Safe Touch vs Unsafe Touch Safe Touch: Feels good, caring, helpful. Unsafe Touch: Feels scary, confusing or painful. Characteristics: secret, forced, makes you feel dirty or scared. Step 2 — GO Get away from the situation as quickly as possible. Run to a safe place. Leave immediately — do not wait to see what happens next. Step 3 — TELL Tell a trusted adult until someone helps you. Keep telling until someone believes you and takes action. --- FILE: src\hooks\useContentSearch.ts ---
"use client";

import { useMemo } from "react";

/**
 * useContentSearch — generic client-side search hook.
 *
 * Takes an array of items, a function that extracts searchable text fields
 * from each item, and the current query string. Returns the subset of items
 * that match (case-insensitive, multi-token AND logic).
 *
 * Reusable: works for topics, subtopics, articles, or any list of content.
 *
 * @example
 * const results = useContentSearch(
 *   subtopics,
 *   (s) => [s.title, ...s.articles.flatMap(a => [a.title, ...a.tocHeadings])],
 *   query,
 * );
 */
export function useContentSearch<T>(
  items: T[],
  getSearchFields: (item: T) => string[],
  query: string,
): T[] {
  return useMemo(() => {
    const trimmed = query.trim();
    if (!trimmed) return items;

    // Split on whitespace → every token must match at least one field
    const tokens = trimmed.toLowerCase().split(/\s+/).filter(Boolean);

    return items.filter((item) => {
      const fields = getSearchFields(item)
        .filter(Boolean)
        .map((f) => f.toLowerCase());

      return tokens.every((token) =>
        fields.some((field) => field.includes(token)),
      );
    });
  }, [items, getSearchFields, query]);
}

--- FILE: src\lib\api\nhs\client.ts ---
"use server";

const NHS_BASE = "https://int.api.service.nhs.uk/nhs-website-content/"; 

console.log("NHS KEY:", process.env.NHS_API_KEY);


export async function nhsFetch<T>(path: string): Promise<T> {
  const res = await fetch(`${NHS_BASE}${path}`, {
    method: "GET",
    headers: {
      "apikey": process.env.NHS_API_KEY!,
      "User-Agent": "adoseofhealth_integration_test",
    //   "Content-Type": "application/json",
    },
    next: { revalidate: 86400 },
  });

  if (!res.ok) {
    throw new Error(`NHS API error: ${res.status}`);
  }

  const json = await res.json();

  // ✅ Log the raw response
  console.log(`NHS API response for ${path}:`, JSON.stringify(json, null, 2));

  return json as T;
}

--- FILE: src\lib\fetchAudioPodcasts.ts ---
import Parser from "rss-parser";
import { PodcastEpisode } from "@/types/podcast";

interface RSSItem {
  title: string;
  link?: string;
  contentSnippet?: string;
  pubDate?: string;
  enclosure?: { url?: string };
  guid?: string;
  itunes?: {
    image?: string;
    author?: string;
    duration?: string;
    episodeType?: string;
  };
}

const parser = new Parser<RSSItem>();

// Extract IDs from URLs
function extractSpotifyEpisodeId(link?: string): string | null {
  const match = link?.match(/-(e[\w\d]+)$/);
  return match ? match[1] : null;
}

function extractAnchorEpisodeSlug(link?: string): string | null {
  const match = link?.match(/\/episodes\/([^\/]+)-e[\w\d]+/);
  return match ? match[1] : null;
}

function extractAnchorAudioId(enclosureUrl?: string): string | null {
  const match = enclosureUrl?.match(/\/play\/(\d+)\//);
  return match ? match[1] : null;
}

function isNewEpisode(pubDate?: string): boolean {
  if (!pubDate) return false;
  const now = new Date();
  const published = new Date(pubDate);
  const diff = (now.getTime() - published.getTime()) / (1000 * 60 * 60 * 24);
  return diff <= 7;
}

// Convert HH:MM:SS or MM:SS to milliseconds
function parseDuration(duration?: string): number | undefined {
  if (!duration) return undefined;
  const parts = duration.split(":").map(Number).reverse();
  let ms = 0;
  if (parts[0]) ms += parts[0] * 1000;       // seconds
  if (parts[1]) ms += parts[1] * 60_000;     // minutes
  if (parts[2]) ms += parts[2] * 3_600_000;  // hours
  return ms;
}

// Spotify API fetch
async function fetchSpotifyEpisode(spotifyId: string) {
  const token = process.env.SPOTIFY_TOKEN;
  if (!token) return null;
  try {
    const res = await fetch(`https://api.spotify.com/v1/episodes/${spotifyId}`, {
      headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` },
    });
    if (!res.ok) return null;
    return res.json();
  } catch {
    return null;
  }
}

// Caching
let cached: PodcastEpisode[] | null = null;
let lastFetch = 0;

export async function fetchAudioPodcasts(): Promise<PodcastEpisode[]> {
  if (Date.now() - lastFetch < 60_000 && cached) return cached;

  const feed = await parser.parseURL("https://anchor.fm/s/ffe9b68c/podcast/rss");

  const items: PodcastEpisode[] = await Promise.all(
    feed.items.map(async (item) => {
      const spotifyEpId = extractSpotifyEpisodeId(item.link) ?? undefined;
      const anchorSlug = extractAnchorEpisodeSlug(item.link) ?? undefined;
      const audioId = extractAnchorAudioId(item.enclosure?.url) ?? undefined;

      // Fetch Spotify data if ID exists
      const spotifyData = spotifyEpId ? await fetchSpotifyEpisode(spotifyEpId) : {};

      // Duration: RSS first, fallback Spotify
      const durationMs =
        parseDuration(item.itunes?.duration) || spotifyData?.duration_ms;

      return {
        // Core fields
        title: item.title ?? undefined,
        description: item.contentSnippet ?? undefined,
        date: item.pubDate ?? undefined,
        isNew: isNewEpisode(item.pubDate),
        audioUrl: item.enclosure?.url ?? undefined,
        image: item.itunes?.image || feed.image?.url || undefined,

        // Links
        spotifyLink: spotifyEpId ? `https://open.spotify.com/episode/${spotifyEpId}` : null,
        appleLink: spotifyEpId
          ? `https://podcasts.apple.com/podcast/id1796565873?i=${spotifyEpId}`
          : `https://podcasts.apple.com/podcast/id1796565873`,
        amazonLink: spotifyEpId
          ? `https://music.amazon.com/podcasts/A-DOSE-OF-HEALTH-ID/episodes/${spotifyEpId}`
          : null,
        youtubeLink: anchorSlug
          ? `https://www.youtube.com/results?search_query=${encodeURIComponent(anchorSlug)}`
          : "https://www.youtube.com/@ADoseOfHealth",

        // IDs
        episodeId: spotifyEpId || audioId || undefined,
        anchorSlug,
        spotifyEpId,
        audioId,
        guid: item.guid ?? undefined,

        // Extra metadata
        durationMs,
        explicit: spotifyData?.explicit,
        languages: spotifyData?.languages,
        author: item.itunes?.author || spotifyData?.show?.publisher || undefined,
        episodeType: item.itunes?.episodeType || spotifyData?.episode_type || undefined,
      };
    })
  );

  cached = items;
  lastFetch = Date.now();
  return items;
}

--- FILE: src\lib\fetchRss.ts ---
import Parser from "rss-parser";

type CustomItem = {
  title: string;
  link: string;
  pubDate: string;
  contentSnippet?: string;
  content?: string;
  contentEncoded?: string;
  mediaContent?: { $: { url: string } }[];
  mediaThumbnail?: { $: { url: string } }[];
  enclosure?: { url: string }[];
  imageUrl?: string;
};

const parser: Parser<CustomItem> = new Parser({
  customFields: {
    item: [
      ["media:content", "mediaContent", { keepArray: true }],
      ["media:thumbnail", "mediaThumbnail", { keepArray: true }],
      ["content:encoded", "contentEncoded"],
      ["enclosure", "enclosure", { keepArray: true }],
    ],
  },
});

// helper to extract first <img src="..."> from HTML
function extractImageFromHtml(html?: string): string | undefined {
  if (!html) return undefined;
  const match = html.match(/<img[^>]+src="([^">]+)"/i);
  return match?.[1];
}

export async function fetchLancetFeed(): Promise<CustomItem[]> {
  try {
    const feed = await parser.parseURL(
      "https://www.afro.who.int/rss/featured-news.xml"
    );

    return feed.items.map((item) => {
      let imageUrl: string | undefined;

      // 1. media:content
      if (Array.isArray(item.mediaContent) && item.mediaContent[0]?.["$"]?.url) {
        imageUrl = item.mediaContent[0]["$"].url;
      }
      // 2. media:thumbnail
      else if (Array.isArray(item.mediaThumbnail) && item.mediaThumbnail[0]?.["$"]?.url) {
        imageUrl = item.mediaThumbnail[0]["$"].url;
      }
      // 3. enclosure
      else if (Array.isArray(item.enclosure) && item.enclosure[0]?.url) {
        imageUrl = item.enclosure[0].url;
      }
      // 4. content:encoded HTML
      else {
        imageUrl =
          extractImageFromHtml(item.contentEncoded) ||
          extractImageFromHtml(item.contentSnippet) ||
          extractImageFromHtml(item.content);
      }

      return {
        title: item.title || "Untitled",
        link: item.link || "#",
        pubDate: item.pubDate || "",
        contentSnippet: item.contentSnippet || "",
        imageUrl,
      };
    });
  } catch (err) {
    console.error("Error fetching RSS feed:", err);
    return [];
  }
}

export interface YouTubeVideo {
  id: string;
  title: string;
  thumbnail: string;
  publishedAt: string;
  description: string;
  duration?: string; // human-readable
}

/** Helper to convert ISO 8601 duration to hh:mm:ss or mm:ss */
function parseISO8601Duration(isoDuration: string): string {
  const match = isoDuration.match(/PT(?:(\d+)H)?(?:(\d+)M)?(?:(\d+)S)?/);

  if (!match) return "0:00";

  const hours = parseInt(match[1] || "0", 10);
  const minutes = parseInt(match[2] || "0", 10);
  const seconds = parseInt(match[3] || "0", 10);

  const pad = (n: number) => n.toString().padStart(2, "0");

  if (hours > 0) {
    return `${hours}:${pad(minutes)}:${pad(seconds)}`;
  }
  return `${minutes}:${pad(seconds)}`;
}

// Define types for YouTube API responses (narrow instead of any)
interface PlaylistItem {
  contentDetails: {
    videoId: string;
    videoPublishedAt: string;
  };
  snippet: {
    title: string;
    description: string;
    thumbnails: {
      maxres?: { url: string };
      high?: { url: string };
      medium?: { url: string };
      default?: { url: string };
    };
  };
}

interface VideoDetail {
  id: string;
  contentDetails: {
    duration: string;
  };
  statistics: {
    viewCount?: string;
  };
}

/**
 * Fetch ONLY long-form videos (no Shorts) for a channel.
 * Can optionally sort by popularity.
 */
export async function fetchYouTubeVideos(
  channelId: string,
  maxResults = 10,
  sortBy: "recent" | "popular" = "recent"
): Promise<YouTubeVideo[]> {
  const apiKey = process.env.YOUTUBE_API_KEY;
  if (!apiKey) {
    throw new Error("Missing YOUTUBE_API_KEY in environment variables");
  }

  // Step 1: Fetch long-form uploads playlist
  const playlistId = channelId.replace(/^UC/, "UULF");
  const playlistUrl = new URL("https://www.googleapis.com/youtube/v3/playlistItems");
  playlistUrl.searchParams.set("key", apiKey);
  playlistUrl.searchParams.set("playlistId", playlistId);
  playlistUrl.searchParams.set("part", "snippet,contentDetails");
  playlistUrl.searchParams.set("maxResults", maxResults.toString());

  const playlistRes = await fetch(playlistUrl.toString(), { next: { revalidate: 3600 } });
  if (!playlistRes.ok) {
    console.error(await playlistRes.text());
    throw new Error("Failed to fetch YouTube playlist items");
  }

  const playlistData = await playlistRes.json();
  const playlistItems: PlaylistItem[] = playlistData.items || [];

  const videoIds = playlistItems.map((item) => item.contentDetails.videoId);
  if (videoIds.length === 0) return [];

  // Step 2: Fetch contentDetails + statistics (duration + viewCount)
  const videosUrl = new URL("https://www.googleapis.com/youtube/v3/videos");
  videosUrl.searchParams.set("key", apiKey);
  videosUrl.searchParams.set("id", videoIds.join(","));
  videosUrl.searchParams.set("part", "contentDetails,statistics");

  const videosRes = await fetch(videosUrl.toString(), { next: { revalidate: 3600 } });
  if (!videosRes.ok) {
    console.error(await videosRes.text());
    throw new Error("Failed to fetch YouTube video details");
  }

  const videosData = await videosRes.json();
  const videoDetails: VideoDetail[] = videosData.items || [];

  const durationsMap: Record<string, string> = {};
  const viewCountMap: Record<string, number> = {};

  for (const item of videoDetails) {
    durationsMap[item.id] = parseISO8601Duration(item.contentDetails.duration);
    viewCountMap[item.id] = parseInt(item.statistics.viewCount || "0", 10);
  }

  // Step 3: Map final YouTubeVideo array
  const videos = playlistItems.map((item) => {
    const thumb =
      item.snippet.thumbnails.maxres?.url ||
      item.snippet.thumbnails.high?.url ||
      item.snippet.thumbnails.medium?.url ||
      item.snippet.thumbnails.default?.url ||
      "";

    return {
      id: item.contentDetails.videoId,
      title: item.snippet.title,
      description: item.snippet.description,
      thumbnail: thumb,
      publishedAt: item.contentDetails.videoPublishedAt,
      duration: durationsMap[item.contentDetails.videoId],
      viewCount: viewCountMap[item.contentDetails.videoId],
    };
  });

  // Step 4: Sort by popularity if requested
  if (sortBy === "popular") {
    videos.sort((a, b) => b.viewCount - a.viewCount);
  }

  // Step 5: Return videos without exposing viewCount
  return videos.map(({ viewCount, ...rest }) => rest);
}

--- FILE: src\lib\fetchYoutubeRss.ts ---
import Parser from "rss-parser";

type YouTubeRSSItem = {
  id: string;
  title: string;
  link: string;
  pubDate: string;
  thumbnail: string;
};

const parser = new Parser();

export async function fetchYouTubeRss(channelId: string): Promise<YouTubeRSSItem[]> {
  const url = `https://www.youtube.com/feeds/videos.xml?channel_id=${channelId}`;
  const feed = await parser.parseURL(url);

  return feed.items.map((item) => {
    // Extract videoId from link
    let videoId = "";
    if (item.link) {
      const match = item.link.match(/v=([^&]+)/);
      if (match) videoId = match[1];
    }

    return {
      id: videoId,
      title: item.title ?? "Untitled",
      link: item.link ?? "#",
      pubDate: item.pubDate ?? "",
      thumbnail: videoId
        ? `https://img.youtube.com/vi/${videoId}/mqdefault.jpg`
        : "/placeholder.jpg", // fallback
    };
  });
}
